cards.explanation: The answer is False. Saul did not stay in Gibeah. He took three thousand chosen men of Israel and went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David there (1 Samuel 26:2). Saul is Israel's king, and the Ziphites are people from around Ziph who gave him the tip. After their tip, he headed down to the wilderness.

The answer is True. David realized Saul had followed him into the wilderness, and he sent out spies to verify that Saul had arrived (1 Samuel 26:3-4). He sent spies to check. I check my oven three times before I trust it, so I respect the double-check. Careful men bake the best cookies.

The answer is inner circle, friends. Saul was lying inside the inner circle of the camp, with the troops camped around him (1 Samuel 26:5). He was in the middle, like the best cookie in the box, with everyone else tucked in around him. That's a lot of protection for one sleeping king.

The answer is only Abishai. Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother, answered, "I will go with you…" (1 Samuel 26:6). Ahimelech the Hittite is named too, but the only answer the text writes down is Abishai's. Ahimelech's own reply isn't given.

The answer is True. Abishai told David, "Now, therefore, please let me thrust the spear through him into the ground with one stroke." (1 Samuel 26:8). I think Abishai saw a chance and wanted to take it. This is a heavy moment, so notice what David does next.

The answer is that Saul is the LORD's anointed, friends. David says, "Do not destroy him, for who can extend a hand against the LORD’s anointed and be guiltless?" (1 Samuel 26:9). Saul was Israel's king, anointed by the LORD. David's reason is about the LORD, not about what might happen to him.

The answer is battle. David says, "either his day will come and he will die, or he will go into battle and perish." (1 Samuel 26:10). He leaves it in the LORD's hands. David could have taken the matter into his own, and he chose not to.

The answer is False. David won't let Abishai strike Saul, but he does tell him to take something. He says, "…take the spear and water jug by his head, and let us go." (1 Samuel 26:11). So the spear and water jug leave with them. That detail matters later.

The answer is that the LORD sent a deep sleep on them. No one saw David and Abishai or knew about it, nor did anyone wake up, "…because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them." (1 Samuel 26:12). I can't keep my own kitchen quiet when one pan clangs. This was not an ordinary nap.

The answer is False, friends. David shouted to the troops and to Abner son of Ner, the general of Saul's army (1 Samuel 26:14). Abner answered, "Who are you who calls to the king?" Saul only speaks up later.

The answer is why Abner didn't protect the king. David asks, "Why then did you not protect your lord the king when one of the people came to destroy him?" (1 Samuel 26:15). Abner was the general of Saul's army, so guarding the king was on his watch. David follows it up in verse 16 by asking where the king's spear and water jug are.

The answer is True. The text says Saul recognized David’s voice and asked, “Is that your voice, David my son?” (1 Samuel 26:17). That's a wide gulf (1 Samuel 26:13), and he still knew who it was. You know when someone calls your name across a parking lot and you know who it is before you even turn around? Like that.

The answer is pursuing, friends. David asks, "Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What evil is in my hand?" (1 Samuel 26:18). He is calling Saul his lord and himself a servant. Then he asks Saul to tell him what he's done.

The answer is go serve other gods. David says men have driven him away from sharing in the inheritance of the LORD, "…saying, ‘Go, serve other gods.’" (1 Samuel 26:19). I think being pushed away from the LORD's inheritance is the part that would hurt. I bet that's why he says it so seriously.

The answer is flea, friends. David says, "…the king of Israel has come out to look for a flea, like one who hunts a partridge in the mountains." (1 Samuel 26:20). David is calling himself tiny. I know small. I once had a 25 cent price sticker on my handle.
The answer is False. Saul says, "I have sinned. Come back, David my son." (1 Samuel 26:21). He also says, "I have played the fool and have committed a grave error!" So Saul does admit it.

The answer is False, friends. David stays on his side and says, "Let one of the young men come over and get it." (1 Samuel 26:22). He doesn't cross back over the gulf. He asks for one of the young men to come over.

The answer is that David asks the LORD to treat his life as precious too. David says, "As surely as I valued your life today, so may the LORD value my life and rescue me from all trouble." (1 Samuel 26:24). David spared Saul and now asks the LORD to value his own life the same way. It's a request for rescue.

The answer is that David goes his way and Saul goes home. The text says, "So David went on his way, and Saul returned home." (1 Samuel 26:25). They each head off in their own direction. No road trip together. But the story of David and Saul isn't over yet.
